newsitem.title: UK: Thorn shares tumble after profit warning.
newsitem.headline: Thorn shares tumble after profit warning.

text.p: Shares in Thorn Plc fell to their lowest level since it split from EMI after the British electrical retailer and rental company warned on Monday that annual profits would be broadly unchanged from last year.

The group, which split from music giant EMI in August 1996, said that profits before tax and one-off items would be roughly in line with last year's pro forma equivalent of 170.7 million pounds ($283.5 million), disappointing a market that had been looking for profits in excess of 180 million pounds.

Profit before tax and exceptional items for the nine months ended December 31 rose eight percent on a pro forma basis to stand at 123.0 million pounds on turnover of 1.19 billion pounds, up five percent.

"The third-quarter figures aren't too disastrous but what they are implying about the fourth quarter takes our forecast down another 10 million or so," said Nick Bubb, an analyst at banking group Mees Pierson.
By 1255 GMT, shares in the company had fallen 40 pence to stand at 211-1/2 pence on heavy turnover of 12.2 million.
Thorn shares recently reached a high of 290 pence but have been in a general downtrend since its demerger from EMI in August when they hit a peak of 409 pence.
"It is not a disastrous earnings shortfall compared to the share price shortfall," said Bubb. "But it does feels a little overdone and its rating could improve if they restore some credibility."

Thorn said fourth-quarter results would be hit by the volume performance over the Christmas season, particularly in its U.S. business, where it noted that electronics retailers had reported a significant drop in store sales over Christmas.
The strength of sterling is also seen taking its toll and the company expects non-UK profits in the fourth quarter to be hit by around 10 percent, or around three million pounds.
"The main reason (for the downturn in U.S. volume growth in December) is related to the consumer electronics market," said Jim Donovan, Thorn's corporate affairs director.
"The electronics sector has been particularly weak driven by the competitive pressures in the states," he added.
Operating profits for the nine-month period in the United States, which accounts for around 40 percent of overall group sales, rose 11 percent, while like-for-like turnover fell five percent.

In Britain, which accounts for around 30 percent of overall sales, operating profits declined nine percent for the nine-month period. Thorn is due to unveil more detailed results for the nine months on February 24.
Thorn's Donovan said its Radio Rentals unit had disappointing results "in particular in relation to the personal computer market."

However, Thorn was pleased with the growth of its new concept Crazy George's chain which had 54 stores in operation by the end of the period. The rent-to-own chain is aimed at cash- and credit-constrained customers.
